sentence: In a network created by people analyzing their understanding of the word (such as ⌊>Wordnet>⌋) the links and decomposition structures of the network are few in number and kind; and include "part of", "kind of", and similar links.

interp.A: "Such as Wordnet" gives an example of a network. "Few in number" and "kind" are coordinated as what the links and structures are. The two clauses before and after the semicolon are joined without an overt conjunction, and the list after "include" coordinates the quoted sequence ("kind" modified by "of") with "similar links".
interp.B: "Such as Wordnet" gives an example of "the word". "In" takes the coordination "number and kind", so the links are few in number and in kind. The two clauses are joined by "and", and "part of", "kind of" form one quoted word sequence ("part" modified by "kind" and "of") coordinated with "similar links" as what the links and structures include.

sentence: Before the ⌊>dissolution of the Soviet Union>⌋, the overwhelming majority of ⌊>Russophone>⌋s in North America were Russian-speaking ⌊>Jews>⌋.

interp.A: "Russophones" is a name used as a bare plural with no determiner, meaning Russophones in general.
interp.B: "Russophones" is a proper name referring to one named entity, with an ordinary proper-name quantifier.

sentence: It measures predictive power of the model i.e. the proportion of the total variation in the dependent variable that is “explained” (accounted for) by variation in the independent variables.

interp.A: "I.e." attaches to the whole measuring clause. The proportion is what is "explained", with "(accounted for)" as a subordinate gloss on it. "By variation in the independent variables" says what does the explaining, and "in the dependent variable" locates the variation.
interp.B: "I.e." attaches to "the model", so the model is glossed as the proportion. The dependent variable is what is "explained", and "accounted for" takes the variation and the model as its arguments, modified by "in the independent variables".

sentence: In ⌊>linguistics>⌋, ⌊∗semantics∗⌋ is the subfield that is devoted to the study of meaning, as inherent at the levels of words, phrases, sentences, and even larger units of ⌊>discourse>⌋ (referred to as ⌊/texts/⌋).

interp.A: "Meaning" is the verb "mean" nominalized (the study of meaning something). "As inherent at the levels..." is a subordinate clause attached to that meaning. "Referred to as texts" describes the larger units, and "even" modifies a noun phrase.
interp.B: "Meaning" is a noun (the study of meaning), and "inherent" is predicated of the study itself. "Even" modifies the comparative "larger", and "referred to" describes "discourse", with "as texts" read as an equative comparison.

sentence: Efficient marketing is a process of understanding the amount of variability and tailoring the marketing strategy for greater profitability.

interp.A: "For greater profitability" modifies "the marketing strategy": a strategy for greater profitability, which is what gets tailored.
interp.B: "For greater profitability" modifies "tailoring": the strategy is tailored in order to get greater profitability.
